status: proven as crash insurance
description: The thesis's index sleeve: hold `symbol` while its 12-month return is positive (checked monthly), otherwise cash.
evidence: SPY 1994-2026: 10.6%/yr vs 10.8% buy & hold, worst drop -34% vs -55%; robust across periods, markets and costs. Cost ~1%/yr in 2014-2026 (fast rebounds).
parameters: symbol=SPY; lookback=252

status: tested, no edge over SPY sleeve
description: Index rotation ("dual momentum"): each month, rank major index funds by momentum (12-month return, or a blend of lookbacks) and hold the best `top` - or, with drop_worst=N, everything except the N weakest. Only funds with positive momentum are held; a failing slot sits in cash (earning T-bills). weighting: equal slices, or "rank" (the leader gets the biggest slice). With symbols=SPY and top=1 this is index_momentum.
evidence: 2004-2026, 6 indices (SPY QQQ IWM DIA EFA EEM): top 2 11.6%/yr, Sharpe 0.60 vs the SPY sleeve 9.4%, 0.58 - more risk, same Sharpe; gains all from 2004-12, relies on QQQ, fragile to lookback; walk-forward 8.3% (0.45) vs 10.2% (0.61). 'Avoid the worst' (drop_worst, rank weights): Sharpe 0.54-0.58, walk-forward 8.0% (0.44). No improvement inside the desk.
parameters: symbols=['SPY', 'QQQ', 'IWM', 'DIA', 'EFA', 'EEM']; top=1; lookback=252; drop_worst=0; weighting=equal; lookbacks=

status: promising, not proven
description: Top 25 of the quality stock screen, equal weight, re-picked every quarter (backtested: quarterly beat annual - research/screen_backtest.py). Positions drift between re-picks; no stop-loss (none was backtested).
evidence: Point-in-time 2014-2026: top 25 re-picked quarterly 17.9%/yr (Sharpe 0.89) vs same-universe 11.4% and SPY 13.8%; edge vs universe t~1.8. Survivors-only prices.
parameters: top=25; rebalance=False; max_age_days=10; rebalance_months=3
notes: Winners study (research/WINNERS.md): across 31 five-year windows, high ROIC / margins / FCF margin and low debt cut the chance of a bust by 20-40% but barely raised the chance of a top-decile winner (1.1-1.5x). Quality is a way to lose less, not to find 10-baggers. A walk-forward composite of all traits did not beat random (hit rate 6% vs 10%).

status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
description: ICT (Inner Circle Trader) day-trading models as fixed rules on the 100 largest US companies: the Silver Bullet (5-min fair value gap after a liquidity sweep, 10-11am New York) and the Judas swing (fade a first-hour fake-out beyond the prior day's high/low), optionally with the quality score choosing the side (long strong companies, short weak ones) or a 50-day trend filter.
evidence: Silver Bullet (60 days, 2,974 trades): +0.01R before costs, -0.06% per trade after (t -3.5). Judas swing (3 years, 21,483 trades): -0.01R, -0.07% after costs (t -10), negative in all 13 quarters. Same as a coin-flip direction. Financial bias, long only, reaches break-even at best; trend filter worse. Re-run on 2016-2026 Alpaca 5-minute bars (222 of 224 top-100 names): Silver Bullet 129,658 trades, +0.02R before costs, -0.051% after (t -21), negative every year; Judas swing 80,366 trades, -0.00R, -0.053% after; both halves.
parameters: target=2R; stop=beyond the sweep; exit=end of day; costs=0.03% each way; universe=100 largest US companies

status: tested, no edge as strategies (not in the live mix)
description: Five documented short-term effects with next-open fills: weekly pullback bought at Monday's open, post-earnings drift after the 10-Q filing, the 52-week high (monthly and swing), overnight vs daytime returns, and the opening range breakout on stocks in play (60-day preview).

status: accepted as the desk's 30% sleeve (amendment 330e76e0) - live from `overnight activate`
